newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister raps CIC banker over gaffe.
newsitem.headline: French minister raps CIC banker over gaffe.

text.p: France's finance minister delivered a rebuke on Thursday to the head of soon-to-be-privatised CIC bank, hinting he might take reprisals against him for an outburst against the bank's main bidders.

CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt told French television on Wednesday that bids drawn up by Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) and Societe Generale could spell the "death" of CIC and its regional banking network.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis used an interview on the same channel on Thursday evening to rap Yoncourt for stepping out of line by discussing the bids mid-way through privatisation.
"It is unacceptable coming from a chairman and I shall draw the consequences," he told all-news LCI television.
Asked to explain what he meant, Arthuis replied, "You will see in coming days."
BNP and Societe Generale are bidding to buy 67 percent of CIC held by state insurance company GAN in a privatisation due to be completed by the end of the year.
In his Wednesday interview, Yoncourt said the offers by the two banks "risk, unless they are contradicted by the facts or by strong undertakings, to be the death knell for CIC."
He added he could not imagine how two banking networks could exist under the same roof while serving "the same towns, the same professions, the same clients."
Asked for a response, Arthuis said the secrecy required during privatisation talks had been broken.
"He committed a fault because the privatisation must be carried out in (conditions of) neutrality and confidentiality," he said.
CIC was not immediately available for comment.
But its state-owned parent GAN issued a statement calling on everyone involved to refrain from any further public comment.
"Until the end of the procedure, GAN will refrain from any declarations or any positions which could influence the outcome," the statement said.
"Based on this principle, it wishes all the players involved, whether inside or outside the group, to show the same discretion and not undermine the natural development of the procedure under way."
Banking analysts have said CIC, a large commercial grouping of 11 regional banks, might have to be rationalised following a sale to a major bank to avoid competing with its buyer.
Shares in the publicly quoted part of GAN rose last week on speculation in a Paris newspaper that the privatisation tender might have to be relaunched.
Financial daily L'Agefi speculated that the government might instead choose to sell off GAN and CIC together.
